_meta.name: Cloris default design rubric
_meta.notes: Six principles × four anchor levels. Per-discipline weight overrides cover product / brand / motion / illustration / ux. Editorial baseline for the Designer module's vision-LLM evaluation; recruiters can override per-brief in the intake wizard's design_rubric chapter. The principles + anchor language carries over from docs/designer-hitl-module-spec.md §3 — settled editorial work.

principles.name: Visual hierarchy
principles.description: How clearly the work guides the viewer's attention. Are primary, secondary, and tertiary elements distinguishable without effort? Does the eye land where it should?

anchors.bad: No discernible hierarchy. Every element competes equally for attention; viewer cannot tell what is primary.
anchors.okay: Hierarchy is present but weak. Distinctions between primary and secondary elements are subtle and require effort to read.
anchors.good: Clear hierarchy. Primary, secondary, and tertiary elements are visually distinct and the eye lands on the intended focal point.
anchors.excellent: Hierarchy is purposeful and confident. Each layer serves a deliberate communication purpose; the work directs attention with precision.

principles.name: Typographic refinement
principles.description: Type choices, kerning precision, line-height discipline, and how typography carries the work's voice. Treats type as a first-class design material, not a fill.

anchors.bad: Type is undifferentiated or default. No evidence of intentional typeface selection, sizing, or rhythm.
anchors.okay: Type is consistent without precision. Choices are workable but not load-bearing for the work's identity.
anchors.good: Type is intentional and well-set. Kerning, leading, and pairing reflect craft; the typography carries voice without effort.
anchors.excellent: Typography is a primary expressive material. Decisive type choices, micro-typography precision, and editorial restraint.

principles.name: Compositional balance
principles.description: Spatial relationships across the canvas. Positive and negative space, alignment, rhythm, and how elements relate as a whole.

anchors.bad: Composition is cluttered or arbitrary. Elements feel placed rather than arranged.
anchors.okay: Composition is workable but predictable. Default grid behavior; no compositional ambition.
anchors.good: Composition is considered. Rhythm and balance are intentional; negative space is used as a positive material.
anchors.excellent: Composition is the design itself. Tension, asymmetry, and pacing are deployed with intent.

principles.name: Color system coherence
principles.description: How color choices relate as a system. Palette discipline, chromatic relationships, and the emotional / functional purpose of color.

anchors.bad: Color is incidental or chaotic. No discernible palette discipline; colors fight each other.
anchors.okay: Color works but isn't a system. Choices are workable; coherence is approximate.
anchors.good: Color is systematic. Palette is clearly defined; relationships between colors are intentional.
anchors.excellent: Color is a structural material. Palette has perspective and decisiveness; chromatic relationships carry the work's identity.

principles.name: Conceptual strength
principles.description: Whether the work expresses an idea beyond its surface. Does it reward extended attention? Is there a sharp underlying concept the visual choices serve?

anchors.bad: No discernible concept beneath the surface. The work executes a brief without proposing a frame.
anchors.okay: Concept is present but generic. The frame is recognizable; not particularly its own.
anchors.good: Concept is sharp and the visual choices serve it consistently. The work has a frame worth holding.
anchors.excellent: Concept is original and the execution makes the concept inevitable. The work proposes something rather than fulfilling something.

principles.name: Craft execution
principles.description: Fit, finish, and the absence of avoidable errors. Spacing precision, edge treatment, alignment discipline, asset preparation.

anchors.bad: Visible craft errors. Misaligned elements, low-resolution assets, or mistreated edges signal indifference to detail.
anchors.okay: Craft is acceptable. Few errors but not particularly precise; finish is workable rather than polished.
anchors.good: Craft is clean. Spacing, alignment, and finish are precise; the work reads as intentional throughout.
anchors.excellent: Craft is at the limit of what the medium allows. Every detail serves the whole; nothing draws attention by being wrong.
